yt.title: 1,000 km of fiber adds at least 9.8 ms of ping #Shorts
yt.description:
Round trip time = 2 x distance / (c / n), with c = 299,792.458 km/s and a typical single-mode fiber group index n of about 1.468 at 1550 nm: 9.8 ms for 1,000 km (in a vacuum it would be 6.7 ms). Real paths add routing, queuing and longer cable routes.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: No matter how good your internet is, a far away server has a minimum ping. Physics sets it.
In optical fiber, light travels about a third slower than in a vacuum, roughly two hundred and four thousand kilometers per second.

scenes.label: round trip over 1,000 km of fiber
scenes.narration: Ping is a round trip. For a server one thousand kilometers away, that is at least nine point eight milliseconds, before any routing or processing.
Real cables are not straight, so real pings are higher. That is why games and websites put servers close to you. How far is your favorite server?
